The liability / black-box problem (opaque decision layer, fault assignment, undefined ceiling)
Building public trust: exposure, experience, error-tolerance asymmetry

nodes.label: Trolley problem as ethics, not engineering
nodes.rationale: Interviewees consistently refuse the trolley framing as an engineering problem: technical logic (data-driven judgment, brake-first) should not be conflated with moral-ethical logic; for a vehicle the answer is simply to brake.
nodes.norm_label: trolley problem as ethics, not engineering

nodes.label: Brake-first: collision avoidance is a vehicle technical problem
nodes.norm_label: brake-first: collision avoidance is a vehicle technical problem

nodes.label: L2 as comfort feature for selling cars (70-80 points)
nodes.rationale: Production L2 (Li Auto, etc.) is a convenience/comfort feature to sell cars, only needs ~70-80 points, and by design does not solve the A-to-B autonomy problem.
nodes.norm_label: l2 as comfort feature for selling cars (70-80 points)

nodes.label: Three short-boards: sensor, controller, model
nodes.norm_label: three short-boards: sensor, controller, model

nodes.label: Four dimensions: law, technology, industrialization cost, public cognition
nodes.norm_label: four dimensions: law, technology, industrialization cost, public cognition

nodes.label: Deploy-first, regulate-later (pilot-first, then converge)
nodes.rationale: China's regulatory pattern: let it run and pilot first, then converge into law once problems surface, rather than fixing law rigidly up front and stifling the industry. Seen as a responsible, conservative-but-progressive posture protecting healthy development.
nodes.norm_label: deploy-first, regulate-later (pilot-first, then converge)

nodes.label: Data-driven models improve but never reach 100 / no defined ceiling
nodes.rationale: The hidden risk: constant model/framework churn (CNN to SLAM to BEV to Transformer to large models to VLA) advertises progress (30 to 80 points) but nobody defines what 100 looks like, so the true ceiling is unknown.
nodes.norm_label: data-driven models improve but never reach 100 / no defined ceiling

nodes.label: Tesla vision-only sensor limits (night, rain, fog, glare)
nodes.norm_label: tesla vision-only sensor limits (night, rain, fog, glare)

nodes.label: Corner cases (low-frequency, high-risk edge scenarios)
nodes.norm_label: corner cases (low-frequency, high-risk edge scenarios)

nodes.label: Shadow-mode learning / imitating the median human driver
nodes.rationale: Models learn from human decisions (Tesla FSD shadow mode); human action is treated as the correct answer. The distribution's tails (aggressive/conservative) wash out and the model converges to the majority/median driving style, so its 'ethics' just mirror aggregate human behavior.
nodes.norm_label: shadow-mode learning / imitating the median human driver

nodes.label: Data augmentation, synthesis and simulation for rare data
nodes.norm_label: data augmentation, synthesis and simulation for rare data

nodes.label: Asymmetric tolerance: human error accepted, machine error is not
nodes.rationale: People accept human mistakes as fate/inevitable but cannot accept that a machine also errs, demanding 100% correctness before allowing deployment.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric tolerance: human error accepted, machine error is not

nodes.label: Higher AV penetration yields more rational driving and lower risk
nodes.norm_label: higher av penetration yields more rational driving and lower risk

nodes.label: Public loss-of-control fear and driver unemployment anxiety
nodes.norm_label: public loss-of-control fear and driver unemployment anxiety

nodes.label: L4-to-L5 barrier: not a linear upgrade
nodes.rationale: L5 (all-scene, no ODD limit) is not reachable by upgrading one L4 car; different fine-grained scenarios (e.g. off-road forest) may require different physical embodiments (legged robots), and no one has all-scene data.
nodes.norm_label: l4-to-l5 barrier: not a linear upgrade

nodes.label: Robotaxi economics: commercial closed-loop and scale effect
nodes.rationale: L4 concentrates in urbanized cities because high density, standardized roads and high-frequency demand let a small fleet close the commercial loop; villages lack the scale effect, so tech doesn't choose to commercialize there first.
nodes.norm_label: robotaxi economics: commercial closed-loop and scale effect

nodes.label: Intercity routes vs high-speed rail and jurisdiction
nodes.norm_label: intercity routes vs high-speed rail and jurisdiction

nodes.label: Government inter-department game: safety vs tech progress
nodes.rationale: Government as a whole won't block AV, but transport-safety departments resist over-rapid rollout while science/economic departments push it to avoid falling behind rivals; the state guards the safety floor and lets both routes develop.
nodes.norm_label: government inter-department game: safety vs tech progress

nodes.label: LiDAR+HD-map (Waymo) vs vision/end-to-end (Tesla) routes
nodes.rationale: Tesla ('brute-force aesthetics', scaling-law, cheap sensors, smart brain, low floor/high ceiling) vs Waymo (sensor-rich, high redundancy, dumb-but-safe, high floor/lower ceiling). The route trade-off remains unsolved, so both survive.
nodes.norm_label: lidar+hd-map (waymo) vs vision/end-to-end (tesla) routes

nodes.label: Safety floor (下限) vs ceiling (上限)
nodes.rationale: Humans want new tech to never fail (high floor = safety) yet also be idealized/perfect (high ceiling). Government forced to choose picks the floor, so higher-redundancy routes get wider operating permission.
nodes.norm_label: safety floor (下限) vs ceiling (上限)

nodes.label: L2 assistance vs L4 autonomy (decision base, redundancy, sensors)
nodes.rationale: L2 is human-anchored with one capability that hands back to the driver; L4 is algorithm-anchored with a Plan B / minimal-risk fallback and hardware+algorithm redundancy, hence very different sensor suites and data dimensions.
nodes.norm_label: l2 assistance vs l4 autonomy (decision base, redundancy, sensors)

nodes.label: L4 redundancy and minimal-risk-condition fallback (Plan B)
nodes.norm_label: l4 redundancy and minimal-risk-condition fallback (plan b)

nodes.label: Carmaker owns the full data set / golden training data
nodes.rationale: Data pipeline is fully automatic (like phone OS updates, pre-authorized at purchase); the carmaker holds the full data superset spanning external environment, actuator, decision, and driver-behavior dimensions, only outsourcing analysis to third parties.
nodes.norm_label: carmaker owns the full data set / golden training data

nodes.label: Near-miss vs collision data capture (golden data)
nodes.norm_label: near-miss vs collision data capture (golden data)

nodes.label: Public disclosure of safety data (China vs US)
nodes.rationale: China: no need to disclose because government is trusted and deemed wiser than the public (民智弱); US: Tesla/Waymo publish safety reports as a constitutional/lobby-driven norm even if few read them.
nodes.norm_label: public disclosure of safety data (china vs us)

nodes.label: EV-transition precedent (undisclosed fires, smooth adoption)
nodes.rationale: China's EV shift saw battery fires/deaths that were never fully disclosed to the public, yet adoption progressed smoothly to high penetration and export strength; used as an analogy for how AV can be rolled out without full transparency.
nodes.norm_label: ev-transition precedent (undisclosed fires, smooth adoption)

nodes.label: New-tech precedent: automobile vs the horse-carriage era
nodes.norm_label: new-tech precedent: automobile vs the horse-carriage era

nodes.label: China: government wiser than public + high public trust in government
nodes.norm_label: china: government wiser than public + high public trust in government

nodes.label: Layered decision module (perception, prediction, planning, control)
nodes.rationale: L4 decision is a layered closed loop: multi-sensor perception input, behavior/intent prediction, FSM decision, path planning, and vehicle-side control execution.
nodes.norm_label: layered decision module (perception, prediction, planning, control)

nodes.label: Ghost-probe: sudden pedestrian dart-out (鬼探头)
nodes.norm_label: ghost-probe: sudden pedestrian dart-out (鬼探头)

nodes.label: Model interpretability / deep-learning black-box problem
nodes.rationale: The biggest bottleneck: rule-based modular stacks are mathematically derivable/explainable, but deep-learning models are opaque parameter fits, so on unseen data the output can't be explained, only the result is visible.
nodes.norm_label: model interpretability / deep-learning black-box problem

nodes.label: Accident liability and responsibility assignment
nodes.rationale: After an accident, reconstructing the event and assigning fault depends on model interpretability and on regulatory standards for responsibility division.
nodes.norm_label: accident liability and responsibility assignment

nodes.label: All lives weighted equally (no passenger vs pedestrian preference)
nodes.rationale: No industry-standard engineering solution for extreme trolley scenarios; firms refuse active collision, minimize total harm, and train weights with all lives equal, never setting different coefficients for occupants vs pedestrians.
nodes.norm_label: all lives weighted equally (no passenger vs pedestrian preference)

nodes.label: Risk grading (distance/speed/collision probability/harm) and conservative avoidance
nodes.norm_label: risk grading (distance/speed/collision probability/harm) and conservative avoidance

nodes.label: Remote operators (RO) and P0/P1/P2 incident grading
nodes.rationale: Incidents are graded P0/P1/P2; remote operators watch via the control platform, SOS/HMI lets passengers reach support, cabin cameras trigger anomaly alerts, and ground/grid crew and 120 ambulance are dispatched within time targets.
nodes.norm_label: remote operators (ro) and p0/p1/p2 incident grading

nodes.label: Robotaxi onboard safety processes (seatbelt, door interlock)
nodes.norm_label: robotaxi onboard safety processes (seatbelt, door interlock)

nodes.label: Policy uncertainty tightening after Wuhan; ops tooling gaps
nodes.norm_label: policy uncertainty tightening after wuhan; ops tooling gaps

nodes.label: Robotaxi comfort/experience advantage over human taxi
nodes.norm_label: robotaxi comfort/experience advantage over human taxi

nodes.label: Wuhan Robotaxi (Luobo Kuaipao) incident
nodes.rationale: The Wuhan event triggered nationwide policy tightening; problems there were mostly complex traffic-environment situations, not the vehicle's own faults, and the fleet's driving style adapted from local human-behavior data.
nodes.norm_label: wuhan robotaxi (luobo kuaipao) incident

nodes.label: Operational Design Domain (可运营域, operational area)
nodes.rationale: AV value is region-dependent; some districts (Nansha, Huangpu) suit robotaxi better than others (Tianhe). Forcing operation outside a suitable ODD causes traffic problems and negates the technology's positive value.
nodes.norm_label: operational design domain (可运营域, operational area)

nodes.label: Need for national universal AV legislation
nodes.rationale: Current rules are local (per Guangzhou district); a higher-level universal national law covering both commercial and personal AV is wanted so operators and carmakers have consistent guidance, otherwise commercial competition threatens public traffic.
nodes.norm_label: need for national universal av legislation

nodes.label: AV law layered on top of general traffic law (additive, not conflicting)
nodes.norm_label: av law layered on top of general traffic law (additive, not conflicting)

nodes.label: Driving skill not degraded by using automation
nodes.norm_label: driving skill not degraded by using automation

nodes.label: Highway L2 relieves fatigue; city driving stays harder
nodes.norm_label: highway l2 relieves fatigue; city driving stays harder

nodes.label: Firms define edge-case rules differently; risk without a common standard
nodes.norm_label: firms define edge-case rules differently; risk without a common standard

nodes.label: Whitelist regulation mechanism (default-deny, prove-then-open)
nodes.rationale: China uses a whitelist: everything is disallowed by default until you prove a capability, then that scope is opened under reasonable conditions; contrasts with the foreign default-allow blacklist. Overall trend is increasingly open, with occasional two-steps-forward-one-back.
nodes.norm_label: whitelist regulation mechanism (default-deny, prove-then-open)

nodes.label: Ring-based phased rollout (outer/middle/inner rings)
nodes.rationale: Guangzhou's tiered policy: accumulate mileage and safe-operation time in an outer ring, then apply to advance inward toward core-city operation; firms 'clear levels' before core districts open.
nodes.norm_label: ring-based phased rollout (outer/middle/inner rings)

nodes.label: Public exposure gap (few robotaxis vs many human cabs)
nodes.rationale: Even the largest fleet (Luobo ~1000-1200 cars in Wuhan) is dwarfed by tens of thousands of human cabs daily, so ridership is wholly disproportionate and true user preference cannot yet be judged.
nodes.norm_label: public exposure gap (few robotaxis vs many human cabs)

nodes.label: POI pickup/dropoff points (bus-stop-like) and user-education gap
nodes.rationale: Robotaxis pick up/drop off only at POI stations (like a bus), unlike human cabs that will bend rules to stop anywhere; the mismatch with user habit becomes the main source of complaints, driven by education/experience gaps, not danger.
nodes.norm_label: poi pickup/dropoff points (bus-stop-like) and user-education gap

nodes.label: China vs US road environment and regulatory philosophy
nodes.rationale: Dense mixed traffic (electric two-wheelers besieging cities) vs sparse US streets pushes Chinese firms toward rule/safety-oriented routes and US firms toward openness/universality; the core difference is the social, road, and public-opinion environment.
nodes.norm_label: china vs us road environment and regulatory philosophy

nodes.label: Core user need: safe, low-cost A-to-B movement
nodes.norm_label: core user need: safe, low-cost a-to-b movement

nodes.label: Robotaxi vehicle platform: SUV (GAC AION V)
nodes.norm_label: robotaxi vehicle platform: suv (gac aion v)

nodes.label: Multi-objective constrained decision optimization
nodes.rationale: Driving decisions are a multi-objective constrained optimization: safety is a hard constraint, traffic rules a strong (slightly flexible) constraint, and efficiency+comfort are optimization objectives maximized only after the constraints hold; no strict A-then-B priority list.
nodes.norm_label: multi-objective constrained decision optimization

nodes.label: Safety as the hard constraint (top priority)
nodes.norm_label: safety as the hard constraint (top priority)

nodes.label: L5 as an AGI / embodied-AI end-state
nodes.rationale: Industry mostly claims L2++, rarely L3-L4, almost never L5; L5's end-state mirrors AGI/physical AI - the model handling arbitrarily complex situations with no human intervention - and whether it is reachable is contested.
nodes.norm_label: l5 as an agi / embodied-ai end-state

nodes.label: Pedestrians exploit AV yielding behavior
nodes.rationale: An under-noticed effect: at unsignalized crossings people predict the AV will yield and walk straight out, behaving differently than with human drivers.
nodes.norm_label: pedestrians exploit av yielding behavior

nodes.label: First-hand experience builds objective public trust
nodes.rationale: Letting more people ride/experience AV replaces the all-powerful-vs-useless extremes with a calibrated, objective judgment of capability, which aids acceptance.
nodes.norm_label: first-hand experience builds objective public trust

nodes.label: VRU (vulnerable road user) emergency braking
nodes.norm_label: vru (vulnerable road user) emergency braking

nodes.label: Public trust and acceptance (心智 / mindshare)
nodes.rationale: The dominant blocker to L5 is not technology but law/regulation and public acceptance/mindshare; riders must trust the tech, capability, and legal framework enough to board without hesitation.
nodes.norm_label: public trust and acceptance (心智 / mindshare)

nodes.label: Downgrade/degradation strategy over binary A/B choice
nodes.rationale: Real dilemmas (e.g. child darting past a green light) are handled by graded degradation - safety can be placed above rules - not a two-option A-or-B trolley choice; unavoidable rare events are labeled edge cases and minimized, never fully eliminated.
nodes.norm_label: downgrade/degradation strategy over binary a/b choice

nodes.label: World model / BEV perception
nodes.norm_label: world model / bev perception

nodes.label: Multi-sensor fusion (LiDAR, radar, camera)
nodes.rationale: AVs sense the world by fusing LiDAR/microwave-radar (distance/obstacles) with cameras (traffic lights, lane lines, pedestrians via visual recognition), combined by on-car or cloud algorithms to emulate human-like vision.
nodes.norm_label: multi-sensor fusion (lidar, radar, camera)

nodes.label: Speed-limit compliance and adaptive-cruise evolution
nodes.rationale: Assist evolved from fixed cruise to adaptive follow to lane-change/overtake, now near human-like; AVs strictly obey posted limits as a rule constraint and won't speed even when human drivers would.
nodes.norm_label: speed-limit compliance and adaptive-cruise evolution

nodes.label: Trusting Autonomous Machines (interactive education project)
nodes.rationale: Public-interest education project; each chapter is a self-contained HTML experience putting a laptop reader inside one hard question so they feel 'when should I trust a machine' before it is explained. Success: reader articulates why L2 does not equal autonomous without being lectured.
nodes.norm_label: trusting autonomous machines (interactive education project)

nodes.label: Design principle: Show, don't lecture
nodes.rationale: The reader feels the 68 meters before reading the number.
nodes.norm_label: design principle: show, don't lecture

nodes.label: Design principle: Diegetic UI
nodes.rationale: HUD elements belong to the car; timestamps/locations are story, not chrome.
nodes.norm_label: design principle: diegetic ui

nodes.label: Design principle: Choices leave marks
nodes.rationale: Every decision changes state the reader sees again at the debrief.
nodes.norm_label: design principle: choices leave marks

nodes.label: Design principle: Data is the drama
nodes.rationale: Real reaction-time, takeover, and liability figures are the payload of every outcome.
nodes.norm_label: design principle: data is the drama

nodes.label: Design principle: Portable by construction
nodes.rationale: One HTML file per chapter, everything inlined, works from file://.
nodes.norm_label: design principle: portable by construction

nodes.label: Chapter 1 - The Night Drive (Can You Trust Your Car?)
nodes.rationale: Real-3D (Three.js) first-person night drive across five beats: human driving (iMessage reaction-time), L2 assistance (who is responsible), the takeover (measured reaction time, automation complacency), choose your car (L0/L2/L4), debrief. Run saved to localStorage cytc.v1.
nodes.norm_label: chapter 1 - the night drive (can you trust your car?)

nodes.label: Chapter 2 - Inside the Machine (machine perception)
nodes.rationale: AR perception overlays: sensor operation (bounding boxes, LiDAR cloud, radar), sensor fusion (weight sliders + AUTO reliability weighting), sensor failure (glare blinds camera, re-weight to LiDAR/radar), fusion decision. Themes: sensor fusion, redundancy, adaptive weighting, graceful degradation.
nodes.norm_label: chapter 2 - inside the machine (machine perception)

nodes.label: Chapter 3 - The Long Tail (proving safety)
nodes.rationale: Reader is a safety evaluator: log review of 10,000 km, classify a near-miss (bug / edge case / acceptable risk), statistical impossibility of proof, recommend under uncertainty. Themes: the long tail, limits of statistical proof, simulation, deciding under uncertainty.
nodes.norm_label: chapter 3 - the long tail (proving safety)

nodes.label: Chapter 4 - Who's Responsible? (liability)
nodes.rationale: Reader is a regulator investigating an L2 crash: reconstruction, three conflicting testimonies, the black box (decision-layer reasoning unreadable so fault can't be assigned), the policy call. Themes: interpretability/black-box, L2 handover liability, transparency-vs-managed-trust. Grounded in the interviews.
nodes.norm_label: chapter 4 - who's responsible? (liability)

nodes.label: Chapter 5 - The Trust Gap (finale)
nodes.rationale: Reader is a city official approving robotaxi deployment: the exposure gap in numbers, fact-check the operator pitch, a community meeting of five resident voices, the decision (approve / phased geofenced / deny) and how to announce it. Themes: real-world exposure as engine of trust, claims-vs-reality, phased/whitelist rollout, transparency.
nodes.norm_label: chapter 5 - the trust gap (finale)

nodes.label: Shared localStorage save cytc.v1 (five-chapter continuity)
nodes.rationale: All five chapters merge-on-write into one cytc.v1 save so choices carry forward; each Continue button tries host sendPrompt then falls back to navigating to the next file, so the arc plays as one flow in a plain browser.
nodes.norm_label: shared localstorage save cytc.v1 (five-chapter continuity)

nodes.label: Statistical impossibility of proving safety (~275M miles, RAND)
nodes.rationale: You'd need ~275 million miles (RAND) just to show with confidence the car is as safe as a human, and billions for real proof no fleet has driven incident-free; the long tail of rare events can never be fully tested.
nodes.norm_label: statistical impossibility of proving safety (~275m miles, rand)
